steps.notes:

At 13.62 and 7.998% (to redo with the Oct 30 yield):
- Trailing 4 quarters DPS about PHP 1.0525 (Q4-25 about 0.2505 + 0.263 + 0.263 + Q3-26 0.2762): yield 7.73%, spread about -27 bps. Q4-25 DPS is derived (cash dividends paid in 1Q26 of PHP 932.3M / 3,722M shares); confirm on PSE Edge.
- Q3 DPS annualised PHP 1.1048: yield 8.11%, spread about +11 bps
Either way the spread is thin. That is the input for the leader's Pillar 2 call.

Q3 2026 results came out Oct 22 (not mid-Nov): revenue PHP 2.71B, distributable income PHP 1.93B, Q3 DPS PHP 0.2762, record Nov 10, payment Nov 20.

steps.title: Write Section 3 (Financial Analysis), self-check it, paste into the team doc
steps.notes:
Write 11:00 to 1:00, self-check 1:00 to 1:30. All numbers from the leader's model, marked [preliminary]. The forecast doesn't change with the leader's valuation fixes, so this is safe to write first.
1. Outlook first: revenue 5,580M (2025) to 8,833M (2026E) and 11,187M (2027E); DPS 1.078 (2026E) to 1.146 (2027E), then +3.2% a year to 2031E.
2. Revenue drivers: Wave 4 (from January) and Wave 5 (from July); Q3 revenue 2.71B (+90%) and distributable income 1.93B (+106%); then 3.2% rent growth, below management's 5% (model uses 4% escalation and 0% reversion; say where we differ and why).
3. Costs and margin: about 76% since 2023, held flat; management says it dips as malls and the hotel come in (Q52), so flag it as under review.
4. Distributable income, payout, cash: 2025 payout 99% and dividends paid (3.72B) above operating cash (3.49B); Q3 payout 91%; the accretion finding.
5. Balance sheet: loan 7.2B; loan / total assets about 6% after the waves; interest cover 8.0x (2025).
6. Ratio table (2023A / 2024A / 2025A / 2026E / 2027E): revenue growth 13.9 / 8.6 / 23.6 / 58.3 / 26.7%; operating margin 75.9 / 76.3 / 76.3 / 76.3 / 76.3%; interest cover 10.3 / 11.3 / 8.0 / 12.7 / 16.1x; loan / total assets 11.7 / 9.5 / 9.4 / 5.9 / 5.8%; DPS check / check / check / 1.078 / 1.146. Don't quote the model's 2026E payout (88%); it's probably about 96% (old share count for 1H).
Self-check: first sentence is a forecast; every past fact followed by what it means for the forecast; every number matches the model, in PHP M; guidance labelled as management's; no adjective without a number. Use distributable income, not the US FFO formula.

steps.notes:
LEADER'S DECISIONS (Nov 3): re-rating story built on our own calculations, not management's answers; 12-month target price, call = Hold with a clear Buy trigger; Buy/Sell cutoffs at cost of equity +/- 5 pts (confirmed); cap rate 8.25%. Pillar 2: suggested move to Risks + Buy trigger (asked the leader; check his answer).

Write 2:00 to 4:00, check 4:00 to 4:30. Lesson 6 in the draft course explains each method. Write the words first and fill in the numbers last, after the leader's model fixes (Oct 30 risk-free 8.134% is in).
1. Method paragraph: why the dividend discount model leads (a REIT must pay out at least 90% of distributable income); why asset value (NAV) and the peer comparison are cross-checks; why we skip P/E (net income swings with appraisal gains and losses); why the cost of equity and not WACC; the reason for the 40/40/20 weights.
2. Assumptions table, a source for every input: price 13.62 (PSE, Oct 30), risk-free 8.134% (Oct 30 10Y BVAL), beta, equity risk premium, cost of equity, long-run growth, cap rate 8.25% (reason: our long-run growth of 2% is slower than the appraisers' 3.4% weighted, 4% for most offices), 2027E NOI, shares (6,356M), peer yields, weights. Mark placeholders as placeholders.
3. Results: NAV per share, dividend model value, peer-yield value, blended value today, the 12-month target and the rating. Take the numbers from the leader's updated model.
4. The valuation gap: appraisers 6.6% (all 12 Wave 5 reports, verified Nov 3), our model 8.25%, market-implied 9.17% on 2027E NOI (about 8.9% on current rent; say which basis). NAV per share 19.32 / 15.25 / 13.62. MREIT's 7.8% is in its Sep 14 press release but the basis isn't stated; most likely NOI before capex reserves on the PHP 27B deal price (unconfirmed, so describe it that way and ask the mentor). Deal price about 6.9% below the PHP 29.0B appraised total.
5. Sensitivity: target price at different costs of equity and growth rates, and at different cap rates; show the % change and the rating in each case.
6. The Buy trigger: full-year 2026 results confirming the higher income per share, or the 10Y below about 7.8% (all else equal).
7. In progress (say so): building-by-building asset value, full peer comparison table, stress tests, Monte Carlo.
Last year's graders asked for: a reason for each method, a peer comparison table, sensitivity in % on the discount rate and growth, and numbers that recompute. Self-check: upside = target / Oct 30 close - 1; share count stated; every number matches the model.
Source flags (don't overstate in the draft): Festive Walk appraisal has odd year-1 costs and the lowest rates of all 12; all 12 reports signed before their valuation dates. Details in 06-mreit-data.md.
